_comment: ignoreCommand decides whether Vercel builds at all: exit 0 skips, exit 1 builds.
It began as `[ "$VERCEL_ENV" != "production" ]`, which skips whenever
VERCEL_ENV is anything but that exact string. That is unsafe twice over: an
empty value skips, and — the case that actually bit us — if the project's
production branch is ever not `main`, a push to main arrives as a PREVIEW and
is skipped silently. A skipped build is indistinguishable from one that never
started, so production stops moving with nothing to see.
The rule is now branch-first: main always builds, whatever Vercel calls the
environment. Only a preview of some other branch is skipped. Everything else
builds, because failing towards a wasted build beats failing towards a
production that silently stops updating. The echo puts the decision inputs in
the build log so the next failure is readable.
github.silent is deliberately false: Vercel's commit statuses are the only
outside-in evidence of what it did with a push to main.
ignoreCommand: echo "ignore-step: VERCEL_ENV=$VERCEL_ENV ref=$VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF sha=$VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA"; if [ "$VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF" = "main" ]; then echo 'main — building'; exit 1; fi; if [ "$VERCEL_ENV" = "preview" ]; then echo 'preview of a non-main branch — skipping'; exit 0; fi; echo 'unrecognised context — building'; exit 1
